Author: Pankaj Purohit
Bench: Pankaj Purohit
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 Criminal Misc. Application No.1662 of 2023
 (Under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.)
Pintu Kumar ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & another ........Respondents

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Present:-
Mr. Vikas Singh Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. T.C. Aggarwal, learned Deputy Advocate General along with  Ms. Lata Negi, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)

By means of this C482 application, applicant has challenged the charge-sheet dated 05.10.2022;
summoning order dated 10.04.2023 and the entire proceedings of Criminal Case No.3960 of 2023,
under Sections 419, 420 & 120B of IPC, pending in the court of 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Dehradun.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.

3. The case of the prosecution, as reflected from the first information report, is that on 20.07.2022,
the examination of SSC MTS was organised by Government of India from 05.07.2022 to 26.07.2022 at ICreate Solutions ICS Chaman Vihar Centre, in the second shift at 11:30 a.m. to 02:30 p.m.
Vikas Kumar, S/o Ganga Paswan, R/o Sarkoti Atnama, Patna Bihar was also participating in the aforesaid exam.
When at the gate of the examination centre, checking was undergoing, examinee was not matched with the Aadhar Card.

When strictly inquired, he told his name Pintu Kumar, S/o Tapeshwar Singh, R/o Chhoriya Post Office Belchhi, District Patna Bihar, the applicant, who was trying to enter into the examination hall to give examination in place of Vikas Kumar, S/o Ganga Paswan and he also accepted that a sum of Rs.20,000/- was agreed to be paid to him for this.

4. On the basis of the aforesaid first information report lodged by Sudhanshu Upadhaya, the Centre In- charge, a chick was lodged on 20.07.2022 against Pintu Kumar and Vikas Kumar under the aforesaid Sections.

5. After investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted on 05.10.2022 against the applicant-Pintu Pintu Kumar vs State Of Uttarakhand & Another on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66015231/
1 Kumar as well as Vikas Kumar under Sections 419, 420 & 120B IPC, on which cognizance was taken and the applicant was accordingly summoned vide order dated 10.04.2023.
6.

entities.text: Pintu Pintu Kumar vs State Of Uttarakhand & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has not participated in the examination but was stopped just before at the gate of the examination hall.
He further submits that applicant has no criminal history and he was implicated only on account of his confessional statement.

Therefore, no case is made out against him and the entire proceedings of the aforesaid criminal case deserve to be quashed.
7.
Per contra, learned State Counsel submits that from bare perusal of the first information report, it appears to be a case of cheating, which is known as Munna Bhai, in common parlance.

He further submits that from the first information report the case is made out against the applicant and it is not a case, where Hon'ble Court should invoke its inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.
8.

Having heard the rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties and having gone through the material available on record, I find force in the submissions made by learned State Counsel that from bare perusal of the first information report, the case under Sections 419, 420 & 120B IPC is made out against the applicant.

9. The argument advanced on behalf of learned counsel for the applicant regarding the fact that applicant was implicated in the matter only on account of his confessional statement, the veracity of this argument, can only be seen at the time of the trial of the case.
This Court while sitting in the inherent powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., is not enjoined with the power to sift the evidence and to examine the record of the case.
That is exclusively in the domain of the trial court.
10. In this view of the matter, I do not find any merit in the C482 application and the same is hereby dismissed.

(Pankaj Purohit, J.) 19.08.2023 AK Pintu Kumar vs State Of Uttarakhand & Another on 19 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66015231/
